entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 302.727: Defines offense of driving a commercial motor vehicle while revoked and establishes misdemeanor and felony penalties.

headings.title: Nonresident commercial driver operation authorization rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes nonresidents with valid out-of-state CDL credentials to operate commercial vehicles.

headings.title: Commercial driver license requirement upon relocating
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial drivers moving into Missouri to apply for state commercial license within deadline.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 302.730: Authorizes nonresidents holding valid commercial driver licenses to operate commercial vehicles and sets relocation rules.

headings.title: Commercial license application information and history
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes required personal information and mandatory ten-year multi-state driving history disclosures.

headings.title: Commercial license expiration terms and renewals
headings.reviewNote: Establishes six-year duration for standard commercial licenses and three-year term for younger or older drivers.

headings.title: Five-year validity for hazardous material endorsements
headings.reviewNote: Limits hazardous materials endorsement duration to five years from TSA security threat approval date.

headings.title: Biennial commercial license for senior school bus drivers
headings.reviewNote: Requires biennial renewal and seven-dollar fifty-cent fee for school bus drivers seventy-five and older.

headings.title: Three-year hazardous materials term and TSA revocations
headings.reviewNote: Caps hazardous materials endorsements at three years for drivers seventy and older and governs TSA revocations.

headings.title: Forty-dollar fee for commercial licenses over three years
headings.reviewNote: Establishes forty-dollar fee for commercial driver licenses issued for terms exceeding three years.

headings.title: Twenty-dollar fee for three-year commercial licenses
headings.reviewNote: Sets twenty-dollar fee for commercial driver licenses issued for periods of three years or less.

headings.title: Twenty-dollar fee for duplicate commercial license
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes twenty-dollar statutory fee for issuing duplicate commercial driver licenses.

headings.title: Director authority to stagger transitional expirations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to stagger expiration intervals and adjust fees during federal transition periods.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline to transfer commercial license
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial drivers establishing Missouri residency to apply for state CDL within thirty days.

headings.title: One-year cancellation for application or test falsification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits licensing or cancels a commercial driver license for one year after discovery of falsified information in an application or test.

headings.title: Lawful presence verification and rulemaking for CDLs
headings.reviewNote: Requires verifying United States lawful presence before accepting CDL applications, bars CDLs for temporary lawful presence, and authorizes chapter 536 verification rules.

headings.title: Nondomiciled commercial driver license and permit rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes nondomiciled CDLs and permits for employed residents of qualifying foreign jurisdictions, matching lawful presence expiration, requiring surrender of other nondomiciled CDLs, and applying standard fees and rules.

headings.title: Foreign jurisdiction exclusion for nondomiciled CDLs
headings.reviewNote: Excludes the fifty United States, Canada, and Mexico from the term 'foreign jurisdiction' for issuing nondomiciled commercial driver licenses or permits.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 14 subsection headings for 302.735 governing CDL applications, expiration terms, hazardous materials and senior school bus renewals, fees, falsification cancellations, lawful presence, and nondomiciled CDLs.

headings.title: Tamper-resistant manufacture and required CDL contents
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes card information including full name, address, description, photograph, and endorsements.

headings.title: Pre-issuance driving record checks across states and CDLIS
headings.reviewNote: Requires obtaining driving record information from NDR, CDLIS, and prior licensing states before issuing a CDL, with full prior-state checks on initial issuance or first renewal.

headings.title: Ten-day issuance notice to CDLIS
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to notify CDLIS within ten days after mailing a commercial driver license with identifying information.

headings.title: Vehicle class, endorsements, restrictions, and record history
headings.reviewNote: Requires CDLs to indicate vehicle class, endorsements, and restrictions complying with federal law and requires the CDL driving record to contain complete prior-state conviction history.

headings.title: Required data elements on commercial instruction permits
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial driver instruction permits to include the same data elements as a CDL and the words 'CDL PERMIT' or 'COMMERCIAL LEARNER PERMIT'.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 302.740 governing tamper-resistant CDL manufacture and contents, pre-issuance record checks, ten-day CDLIS notice, class/endorsement/history requirements, and commercial learner permit elements.

headings.title: Application of chapter 577 chemical testing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Applies chapter 577 testing procedures without requiring prior formal arrest for commercial drivers.

headings.title: Commercial driver implied consent to chemical testing
headings.reviewNote: Deems commercial vehicle operators to have consented to breath, blood, saliva, or urine testing.

headings.title: Officer authority to direct commercial chemical tests
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes officers to direct chemical tests upon reasonable belief driver has alcohol or drugs.

headings.title: Limitation to two chemical tests per incident
headings.reviewNote: Limits commercial implied consent to not more than two tests arising from same incident.

headings.title: Tested commercial driver right to full test information
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees tested commercial drivers access to complete technical information concerning test results.

headings.title: Admissibility of chemical analysis in court
headings.reviewNote: Makes chemical test results admissible in criminal and administrative proceedings without physician privilege.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 302.745: Establishes commercial driver implied consent to chemical testing for alcohol and drugs, procedures, and admissibility.

headings.title: Admissibility of refusal and officer sworn report
headings.reviewNote: Makes test refusal admissible and requires officer to file sworn report with director of revenue.

headings.title: Officer warning of out-of-service and disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Requires warning that refusal triggers 24-hour out-of-service order and minimum one-year disqualification.

headings.title: Director duty to disqualify upon refusal
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to enter commercial driving disqualification upon receipt of officer sworn report.

headings.title: Court of record hearing on commercial test refusal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes driver to petition court of record to review officer reasonable grounds and refusal.

headings.title: Court order to reinstate commercial driving privilege
headings.reviewNote: Requires judge to order commercial privilege reinstatement if issues are not proven affirmative.

headings.title: Docket priority for commercial test refusal review
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that requests for judicial review of commercial refusals go to head of court docket.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 302.750: Governs commercial chemical test refusals, warnings, officer sworn reports, disqualifications, and circuit court hearings.

headings.title: One-year commercial disqualification for first offenses
headings.reviewNote: Mandates one-year disqualification for driving under influence, vehicular manslaughter, or leaving scene.

headings.title: Three-year disqualification for hazardous material violations
headings.reviewNote: Extends mandatory disqualification to three years if violation occurred while transporting hazardous materials.

headings.title: Lifetime disqualification for repeat major violations
headings.reviewNote: Imposes lifetime commercial disqualification for two or more major driving violations with reduction rules.

headings.title: Lifetime disqualification for controlled substance felony
headings.reviewNote: Mandates permanent unmodifiable lifetime CDL ban for felony drug manufacturing or distribution.

headings.title: Disqualification for multiple serious traffic violations
headings.reviewNote: Imposes sixty-day disqualification for two serious traffic violations and 120 days for three violations.

headings.title: Twenty-four hour out-of-service order for alcohol
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate 24-hour out-of-service order for commercial driver with any measurable alcohol.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for driving while out of service
headings.reviewNote: Classifies operating commercial vehicle during 24-hour out-of-service period as class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: First violation of out-of-service order disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies driver for first out-of-service order violation in accordance with federal regulations.

headings.title: Second violation of out-of-service order disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies driver for second out-of-service violation within ten years under federal rules.

headings.title: Three-year disqualification for third out-of-service violation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates three-year disqualification for third out-of-service order violation within ten years.

headings.title: Out-of-service disqualification for hazardous passenger transport
headings.reviewNote: Imposes 180-day disqualification for violating out-of-service order while hauling hazardous cargo or passengers.

headings.title: Three-year disqualification for repeat hazardous transport
headings.reviewNote: Imposes three-year disqualification for repeat out-of-service violations with hazardous cargo or passengers.

headings.title: Disqualification for other federal regulation offenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial disqualification for any other offenses specified by federal regulations.

headings.title: Ten-day notice to licensing authority and CDLIS
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to update records and notify CDLIS and home state within ten days of disqualification.

headings.title: Cancellation of license and retesting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Cancels commercial license during disqualification and mandates full retesting upon reapplication.

headings.title: Disqualification upon federal imminent hazard determination
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to disqualify commercial driver upon federal determination of imminent safety hazard.

headings.title: Disqualification for failure to appear or pay
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies commercial driver for failure to appear or pay traffic citations until proof of compliance.

headings.title: Consecutive application of multiple disqualification periods
headings.reviewNote: Requires commercial disqualifications to run consecutively unless arising from the same incident.

headings.title: Unreducible lifetime ban for human trafficking
headings.reviewNote: Mandates unreducible lifetime CDL disqualification for felony severe forms of trafficking in persons using a commercial motor vehicle; source footnote notes U.S.C. 7102(11)* appears to refer to 22 U.S.C. Section 7102(11).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 19 subsection headings for 302.755 governing commercial driver disqualification grounds, out-of-service orders, federal hazard and FTA disqualifications, and lifetime trafficking bans; source footnote notes U.S.C. 7102(11)* appears to refer to 22 U.S.C. Section 7102(11).

headings.title: Civil penalty for driver out-of-service order violation
headings.reviewNote: Subjects commercial drivers violating out-of-service orders to federal civil penalties.

headings.title: Civil penalty for employer out-of-service violations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects employers permitting out-of-service or railroad crossing violations to federal civil penalties.

headings.title: Commission chief counsel civil enforcement action
headings.reviewNote: Requires the chief counsel to the state highways and transportation commission to bring civil penalty recovery actions under section 390.156 against violating drivers or employers.

headings.title: Application to intrastate passenger motor vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Applies out-of-service civil penalties to intrastate passenger vehicles carrying over five passengers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 302.756: Establishes civil penalties for drivers and employers violating out-of-service orders and enforcement by commission counsel.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority under CDL act
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director of revenue to adopt administrative rules under section 536.024 for commercial drivers.

headings.title: Approval of state college driving instruction programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to adopt rules approving commercial driving programs at state colleges and universities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 302.765: Authorizes director of revenue rulemaking under commercial driver act and approval of college training programs.

headings.title: Federal motor carrier driver self-certification categories
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to self-certify under interstate or intrastate excepted and nonexcepted categories.

headings.title: Mandatory denial for failing self-certification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Mandates denial of commercial license or permit if applicant fails to certify under an authorized category.

headings.title: Medical examiner certificate documentation and retention
headings.reviewNote: Requires medical certificates or variances for nonexcepted drivers and mandates three-year state retention.

headings.title: Requirement to maintain updated medical certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires nonexcepted commercial drivers to maintain valid medical certificates to retain commercial privileges.

headings.title: Ten-day posting of medical certification to CDLIS
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to post medical certificates, variances, and self-certifications to CDLIS within ten days.

headings.title: Not-certified status update and sixty-day CDL downgrade
headings.reviewNote: Directs state to update status to not certified upon certificate expiration and require downgrade within sixty days.

headings.title: Department rulemaking authority for medical status
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department regulations establishing administrative criteria and fees for medical status updates.

headings.title: One-year commercial license cancellation for falsification
headings.reviewNote: Imposes one-year commercial license cancellation for submitting falsified medical certification information.

headings.title: Director rulemaking authority and nonseverability clause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative regulations under chapter 536 nonseverability for medical self-certification.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for 302.768: Governs commercial driver medical self-certifications, medical examiner certificates, CDLIS posting, and status updates.

headings.title: Prohibition on wanton driving and controlled substances
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits driving commercial vehicle with wanton disregard for safety or under controlled substances.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies general violations of Uniform Commercial Driver's License Act as class B misdemeanors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 302.780: Prohibits wanton driving and driving under controlled substances in commercial vehicles, and prescribes class B misdemeanor penalties.
